plan.summary: This 4-week block starts a 12-week off-camp boxing S&C cycle with one short weekly session built around power first, then simple strength, then brief trunk and neck work. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main lower-body lift so future loading can be adjusted cleanly, and the main build work starts in Week 2. Because sparring is a priority and you only have one 45-minute gym session each week, volume stays tight and focused while keeping strength, power, and speed qualities moving forward.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general lower-body power and foundational strength with simple, repeatable work that does not clash with boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Push the main strength and power lifts a bit harder while keeping weekly fatigue low enough for quality boxing work.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and express it faster with sharper ballistic and jump work suited to boxing.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can and stick the landing softly. Full reset between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a box height you can land on cleanly without tucking hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Start from a controlled quarter squat and jump without a dip.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with small jumps in load, then work up to one hard top set of 3-5 reps with clean form. This establishes your baseline for future squat loading, so stop before technique breaks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your squat max for later training.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the load and reps from your top clean set.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if front-rack positioning is comfortable and squat depth is better there.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Good option if shoulder mobility makes back squat awkward.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Use a controlled pull and squeeze at the top. Leave 2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Brace hard and avoid twisting through the torso.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Keep the chest tall and do not turn it into a shrug.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Move slowly out, keep ribs down, and stop before the low back arches.

substitutionOptions.name: Stability Ball Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Easier option if the ab wheel is too hard to control.

substitutionOptions.name: Cable Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a strong brace and full trunk flexion.

exercises.notes: Use a very light plate or manual resistance. Smooth reps only and stop if the neck feels irritated.

substitutionOptions.name: Quadruped Neck Flexion Isometric
